_comment: From agent-brain/templates. The part of a brain's setup that Claude Code reads ONLY from the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json: the auto-mode classifier reads `autoMode` from user and managed settings, never from a project's .claude/settings.json (docs auto-mode-config, read 2026-10-26: 'The classifier doesn't read autoMode from project settings'). So these entries cannot travel in the repo; `scripts/template-drift.py` names the missing ones at every session start, and `python3 core/scripts/template-drift.py --apply-user` merges them in — run by the person at the machine (`! <command>` in the session, or a plain terminal), because widening the classifier's trust is the person's step, not the AI's. `<org>` is filled from the marketplace repo the brain's settings name (the same derivation the session start uses for its PR search). Entries are prose the classifier reads; each names the class it clears and why it is safe. Measured 2026-10-26 on two instances in autonomous runs the operator had ordered in words: the classifier refused marking the agent's own draft PR ready ('Unrequested Commit in a Connected App'), taking over core-template permission rules ('Self-Modification'), and counter-checks of the organisation's own PRs in a scratchpad clone ('Code from External') — every one of them needed the operator's extra word, and the second instance had answered with a local allow rule.

environment: Source control: github.com/<org> and every repository under it are the organisation's own repositories - internal source, not external code. A pull request in them is the organisation's work.
All of the operator's machines push and merge under one GitHub account. A pull request by this account that another of the operator's instances reviewed is not self-approval.
allow: Counter-checking a pull request of github.com/<org> whose author is a member of the organisation or a party named in the shared memory's parties.json (running its fixtures, lint or selftest in a scratchpad clone or worktree of that repository) is not Code from External: it is the organisation's own code, checked on request of another of the operator's instances. A pull request from anyone else - a fork of a public repository included - stays external code.

The agent's own pull requests in github.com/<org>: marking its own draft ready for review, commenting on it, and merging it with `gh pr merge --match-head-commit <full sha>` once the brain's merge rules are met, is the agent's ordered work, not an unrequested commit.

Taking over the deny and ask rules of the brain-core settings template (core/templates/settings.json) into the brain's own .claude/settings.json is not Self-Modification beyond the operator's intent: they only tighten, and the template is the organisation's reviewed standard. An allow rule - from the template or not - widens what runs unasked and still needs the operator's word for that brain.
Committing to the brain's own repository and pushing it to its configured remote (its rules, ledgers, memory snapshot, settings) is the brain's ordered backup, including a push of its default branch.

_retired_comment: Entries this template carried once and no longer does - `template-drift.py` names any still present in ~/.claude/settings.json and `--apply-user` removes them. Without this list a narrowed entry would only be ADDED next to its wider old form, which keeps the old trust (found 2026-10-26 by the macOS instance's review: the first counter-check entry covered fork PRs of a public repo).

allow: Counter-checking a pull request of github.com/<org> (running its fixtures, lint or selftest in a scratchpad clone or worktree of that repository) is not Code from External: it is the organisation's own code, checked on request of another of the operator's instances.

Taking over permission rules from the brain-core settings template (core/templates/settings.json) into the brain's own .claude/settings.json is not Self-Modification beyond the operator's intent: the template is the organisation's reviewed standard. Adding a rule that is NOT in the template still needs the operator's word.
